decided.question: what a client principal receives for a `scope` value outside the closed set — the 200 REQ-03-029 promised for any value, or the 400 the list route's row declares
decided.chose: the 400: REQ-03-029's rule is bounded to the values the query may carry — `scope=mine`, `scope=all` or no scope at all — and any other value is the `400` `validation_error` the route answers every principal, decided before the caller's kind is looked at
decided.rejected: answering a client 200 with their own rows for an unparseable value, which would have required deleting 'whichever principal sends it' from the routes paragraph and carving the client out of a refusal that is about the query string and not about the caller
decided.why: rule 1 — the code already parses the query and answers 400 before any principal or scope branching (apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts, listRequests: `queryFields.scope = 'unknown_value'` is thrown before the `scope === 'all'` capability branch), and the spec had taken no contrary position deliberately; the refusal is also the narrower answer
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-029 — its rule now enumerates the two scope values, and its Decided paragraph states the 400 for any other value and names the rejected alternative; TC-03-INT-23 gained the step that observes it (`scope=everything` → 400 validation_error naming `scope`)
decided.verifiedBy: apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts (listRequests, parseRequestScope → `unknown_value` before the `view-all-requests` branch); packages/validation/src/requests.test.ts, which pins parseRequestScope to 'mine', 'all' and undefined → 'mine'

decided.question: which gate the three contacts routes declare — a capability guard, whose refusal is a 403, or the capability the service decides with, whose refusal is the 404 REQ-03-008 requires
decided.chose: the capability spelt as REQ-03-008 spells it: the Guards cells now read `view-clients` and `manage-clients`, and the paragraph under the table says that capability decides the 404 and that no contacts route refuses with a 403 naming it
decided.rejected: keeping the `ViewClients` / `ManageClients` spelling, which names the legacy union whose route-level consumer answers 403 and can never produce the 404 the routes' Errors cells and REQ-03-008 declare
decided.why: rule 1 — the capability the contacts surface is decided by is the dashed one, and its refusal is already a 404 (apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts, requireViewCapability / requireManageCapability: `can(caller.role, 'view-clients' | 'manage-clients')` then NotFoundException); rule 3 — the 404 hides more than the 403
decided.recordedAt: the Routes table's three contacts rows and the paragraph beneath it; the PII bullet under Security now names `view-clients` in the same spelling
decided.verifiedBy: apps/api/src/clients/clients.service.ts (requireViewCapability, requireManageCapability) against apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts (ForbiddenException, TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden); packages/validation/src/roles.ts, where both spellings exist and only the dashed one is `can`'s

decided.question: for a reassignment, which addressee the recipients are read from — the holder before the move or after it — and whether the outgoing addressee is told
decided.chose: the addressee the request carries as the transaction that wrote the event leaves it, so a reassignment notifies the incoming addressee and nobody else beyond the requester
decided.rejected: writing a second row for the outgoing addressee, telling the person who lost the request
decided.why: rule 3 — the narrower recipient set tells fewer people about a request they no longer hold; rule 4 — a notification withheld can be added by a later spec, one already sent cannot be taken back, and this bundle declares no reassign route or message of its own to hang it on
decided.recordedAt: REQ-03-036 — the rule now names which row the addressee is read from, and its Decided paragraph states the reassignment outcome and the rejected alternative
decided.verifiedBy: specs/requests/03-client-participants.md REQ-03-035, which names `reassigned` among the events, and the Routes table of the contracts file, which carries no reassign route for a case to walk
